plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid). In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since there's no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $18, I should bid exactly $18 to maximize expected profit.

In this second-price auction format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid between my value and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With value = $39, I should bid $39 to maximize expected profit.
